answer: An agent economy blunts Sybil attacks by pricing each identity with a bonded stake whose yield decays faster than linearly per address, so splitting balance across many wallets loses money. A fresh identity must post the same minimum bond and survive the next consensus pulse before earning credit, and new addresses enter a bounded cohort each epoch, capping injection. Colluding wallets also pay for duplicate work: attestations are matched against independent graders, so a fake ocean cannot self-vouch. Like a comet, each cohort leaves a trail, making mass registration costly.
